story_review.one_viewing_summary: A small restaurant's only server walks out, the phone rings and a diner waits. An AI host panel named Haniya goes up instead of a job ad. A guest scans a table code, taps chow mein and pays, and only then does the kitchen printer fire and the wok flare. The owner's $9,650 a month savings are stamped as his own count with no receipts. Tips stream into a jar at the kitchen pass, which a federal rule allows for cooks only without a tip credit, and the restaurant's own box stays a question mark. One customer finds QR ordering unsuitable. The panel takes the next order while the tip jar hangs under owner says and no record shown tags.
story_review.opening_to_ending: Opening question at 0 to 7 s: with the server gone, who takes the order? It is answered at 51.2 s when the panel takes the order. The closing image (53.6 to 57.4 s) adds the honest limit on the tips. The chain is causal and source-limited, and no outcome beyond the reports is invented.
story_review.weakest_transition: 50.4 to 50.6 s. The cut from the s9 table, where a black-screened phone sits beside the quote card, to the wide panel and pass view. The failed-scan beat ends on a dead screen with no resolved human response, so the return to software taking the order lands without the contrast it sets up.
